t:
(a) 
General Rule.—Subsection (b) of section 528 (relating to tax imposed with respect to certain homeowners associations) is amended to read as follows:


“(b) 
Tax Imposed.—A tax is hereby imposed for each taxable year on the homeowners association taxable income of every homeowners association. Such tax shall be equal to 30 percent of the homeowners association taxable income.”.



 
    (b) 
Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1980.

fable.w: This section only sets a 30 percent tax rate on homeowners association taxable income and gives an effective date. The tempting reading is that mentioning homeowners associations, which are outside parties, signals participation, but they are only the subjects of the tax and are not consulted or given any role in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
fable.s: A tax is hereby imposed for each taxable year on the homeowners association taxable income of every homeowners association.

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a tax rate for homeowners associations and specifies its effective date. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The imposition of a tax is a unilateral government action, not a participatory process.
qwen_block.s: A tax is hereby imposed for each taxable year on the homeowners association taxable income of every homeowners association. Such tax shall be equal to 30 percent of the homeowners association taxable income.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the tax applies to homeowners associations (private entities), there is some form of interaction or participation. However, the text merely defines a tax liability and its effective date. It does not require the government to consult with these associations, nor does it grant them a role in the decision-making process (such as an advisory board or comment period). The relationship is purely regulatory/fiscal, not participatory.

opus.w: This section only changes the tax rate on homeowners association taxable income and sets an effective date. It might seem tempting because homeowners associations are outside the federal government, but here they are just the ones being taxed. Nothing in the text has them, or anyone else outside the government, take part in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a tax on homeowners associations. It does not require the government to consult with these associations or any other outside parties before making a decision. It does not establish an advisory committee, public hearing, or comment period. The mere application of a law to private entities does not constitute participation in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: A tax is hereby imposed for each taxable year on the homeowners association taxable income of every homeowners association. Such tax shall be equal to 30 percent of the homeowners association taxable income.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the tax applies to homeowners associations (private entities), there is some form of interaction or participation. However, the definition of participation requires the government to consult or coordinate with outside parties *before* making a decision, or to grant them a right to sue/object. This section simply imposes a tax liability. It does not involve any consultation, advisory boards, public hearings, or comment periods. The homeowners associations are subjects of the regulation, not participants in the decision-making process.
